title: In repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/feature-compose.ts, stop a failed compose attempt from erasing the durable evi
description:
In repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/feature-compose.ts, stop a failed compose attempt from erasing the durable evidence of an earlier successful one.

Around line 5979-5988 there is a block that begins with this exact comment:

  // Persist the compose report as a durable artifact (mirrors gap-to-feature's PROPOSALS_DIR reports). Never fails the compose.

Inside it, the report is written with:

    writeFileSync(
      join(reportDir, `${pointer.gap?.id ?? "adhoc"}-compose-report.json`),

The filename is keyed only on the gap id, so EVERY attempt overwrites the previous one. Measured 2026-09-03: gap route-edit-4e324cb6 landed commit 0bf96df on origin/dev at 07:09:39, and the report file for that gap now has mtime 07:21:13 with verdict UNFAVORABLE and no new_git_sha, because a later failed retry clobbered it. The evidence that the work succeeded was destroyed by the attempt that came after it. A downstream reconciler in goal-host-vessel reads exactly this file, requires verdict FAVORABLE plus a cutover carrying new_git_sha, and therefore now grades a genuinely-landed edit as not-reached.

Make this change: extract the report path into a local const first. Then, before writing, if the verdict of THIS attempt is not "FAVORABLE" and a report file already exists at that path, read and JSON.parse the existing file; if the existing report has verdict === "FAVORABLE" and its cutovers array contains an entry whose result.new_git_sha is a non-empty string, then do NOT overwrite it — instead write this attempt's JSON to a sibling path with "-attempt-<timestamp>" inserted before the ".json" extension, so the successful report survives. In every other case keep the current behaviour and write to the original path exactly as now.

Wrap the read-and-parse of the existing file in its own try/catch so that a corrupt or unreadable prior report falls back to the current overwrite behaviour rather than throwing. The whole block is already inside a try/catch whose comment says persistence failure must never fail the compose - preserve that property.

Note the sibling filename must NOT end in "-compose-report.json", because other resolvers scan the proposals directory for files with that exact suffix and must not pick up the preserved failed attempts.

Change only this one file.
